title: Senior Compliance Specialist
description: Senior Compliance Specialist Position Description SingleStore is building a real-time data platform that helps organizations transact, analyze and act on data in a single system. We are committed to operating with strong security, privacy and resilience standards across our products, services and internal operations. We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Senior Compliance Specialist to help scale our security, privacy and compliance programs. This role will be responsible for maintaining key certifications, driving cross-functional compliance initiatives, overseeing development and management of our privacy program, supporting compliance with the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), and helping mature our Business Continuity Management System (BCMS). The ideal candidate is practical, organized and collaborative, with experience translating regulatory and framework requirements into durable operational processes across technical and business teams. Job Responsibilities Support governance activities across the security, privacy and compliance program, including maintaining Information Security Management System documentation, evidence, policies, procedures and audit trails. Help maintain and improve active certifications and attestations such as ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA and PCI DSS, while coordinating with stakeholders across the business to ensure ongoing compliance. Drive readiness efforts for new compliance objectives, certifications and customer-driven assurance requirements. Participate in enterprise risk management activities, including risk methodology, risk assessments, treatment planning and follow-up with risk owners. Oversee the development, implementation and ongoing management of SingleStore’s privacy program in partnership with Legal, Security, IT and business stakeholders. Support compliance with applicable privacy and data protection requirements, including operationalizing controls and processes needed to meet regulatory and contractual obligations. Lead and coordinate DORA-related compliance activities, including control mapping, gap assessments, remediation tracking, evidence collection and cross-functional readiness planning. Help develop, maintain and mature the company’s Business Continuity Management System (BCMS), including associated governance, documentation, testing coordination and continuous improvement activities. Support vendor risk and third-party security management activities. Help define corrective action plans and track remediation of audit findings, non-conformities and control gaps with accountable owners. Contribute to security and compliance awareness initiatives and internal training efforts. Partner closely with Legal to support regulatory, contractual and policy compliance obligations across the business. Communicate compliance priorities, expectations and status clearly to technical, business and executive stakeholders. Basic Qualifications 3+ years of experience in security, privacy or compliance. 2+ years of experience working for an Independent Software Vendor, SaaS provider or other technology company. Strong understanding of security and compliance frameworks and regulations such as ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, CCPA and DORA. Experience with compliance operations, audits, risk management processes and control-based programs. Experience coordinating cross-functional workstreams and driving follow-through across engineering, IT, legal and business teams. Working knowledge of cloud technologies and managed service environments. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting compliance for managed cloud services or regulated technology environments. Experience building or operating a privacy program, business continuity program or related governance framework. Experience with DORA, business continuity, resilience, incident response governance or operational risk programs. Familiarity with and ability to support compliance initiatives related to the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 and other emerging AI governance, risk and compliance frameworks. Familiarity with customer-facing compliance topics such as questionnaires, due diligence reviews and contractual security requirements. Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISA, CISM, CIPM, CIPT, CDPSE or ISO 27001 Lead Implementer/Lead Auditor. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Business or a related field. Demonstrated ability to work effectively across engineering, product, IT, sales, legal and executive leadership. title: AI Governance Specialist, Officer
description: Who we are looking for. State Street Alpha is seeking a motivated individual who can support the governance, oversight, and responsible adoption of AI technologies across the organization. This position offers the opportunity to collaborate with architecture, engineering, security, compliance, product, and FinOps teams to help ensure AI solutions align with enterprise governance, security, risk, and cost management standards. Ideal candidates are enthusiastic about emerging AI technologies, cloud platforms governance frameworks, and operational cost management, and are eager to contribute to the development of scalable secure, and cost-effective AI practices Why this role is important to us. The team you will join is part of Charles River Development (or CRD), which became part of State Street in 2018. CRD creates enterprise investment management software solutions for large institutions in institutional investment, wealth management, and hedge funds. Together we have created the first open front-to-back platform - State Street Alpha, that was launched in 2019. As AI adoption continues to accelerate across the enterprise, governance, architectural oversight, and cost transparency are critical to ensuring solutions are secure, compliant, scalable, and operationally sustainable. This role will support the responsible evaluation, onboarding, governance, and consumption management of AI solutions and services while helping teams align to enterprise standards, financial accountability, and strategic objectives. What you will be responsible for As a candidate for this position you will: Support governance reviews and assessments for AI solutions, platforms and services. Collaboratewith cross-functional teams including architecture, engineering, security, compliance, legal, risk management, and FinOps teams. Assist in the developmentand maintenance of AI governance standards, processes, and documentation. Evaluate AI technologies and services against enterprise governance, security, compliance, operational, and cost management requirements. Support AI consumption governance activities including monitoring model utilization, licensing usage, token consumption, and AI operational spend. Assist with identifying AI cost optimization opportunities and governance controls to support responsible usage of enterprise AI platforms and services. Contribute to tracking and reporting AI platform usage metrics, trends and governance compliance activities. Participate in governance reviews related to AI model usage, third-part AI services, Generative AI tooling, and AI-enabled development platforms. Provide coordination and administrative support for governance meetings, architecture reviews, and action tracking. What we value Ability to work well with multiple priorities and effectively handle concurrent demands to prioritize responsibilities. Interest in AI technologies, cloud platforms, governance, enterprise architecture, and FinOps practices. Ability to collaborate effectively with architecture, engineering, security, compliance, operational, and financial management teams. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to operational and cost efficiency. Ability to analyze usage trends, consumption metrics, and governance data to support decision-making. Ability to document processes, governance decisions, standards, and technical information clearly. Self-driven mindset with a willingness to learn emerging AI technologies, governance frameworks, and cost optimization practices. Education & Preferred Qualifications Bachelor's degree in a Technical or Analytical field or equivalent experience. Demonstrated Interest in AI Technologies, cloud service providers, governance, enterprise architecture, or FinOps practices. Foundational understanding of AI concepts including Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), and AI service consumption models. Knowledge of cloud service providers such as Microsoft Azure, and Amazon Web Services. Familiarity with reporting, dashboarding, or cost management tools is preferred. Understanding collaboration and documentation tools such as Jira, Confluence, ServiceNow, or similar platforms is preferred. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. title: Manager, SEO AEO
description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. About the Role Veeam is evolving beyond data protection into a broader platform spanning data security, identity, and AI trust. We are looking for a Manager, AEO/SEO to help lead the strategy, execution, and team responsible for organic discovery across traditional search, AI answer engines, and generative search experiences. This person will play a key role in shaping how Veeam shows up across Google, AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, Claude, and other emerging discovery platforms. The role requires a leader who can combine enterprise SEO maturity, AI search strategy, technical depth, analytical rigor, and team leadership This is a strategic and hands-on role. The right person will be able to translate strategy into clear execution plans, guide team priorities, partner closely with agency resources, support KPI development, and drive work across web, content, product marketing, comms, campaigns, analytics, and technical teams. The goal is to make Veeam more discoverable, more authoritative, more citable, and more recommended across the places where enterprise buyers now search, compare, and make decisions. What You’ll Do Lead SEO/AEO Strategy and Roadmap: Define and lead Veeam's global SEO, AEO, and AI search strategy — translating business priorities into measurable organic discovery programs across markets, personas, product lines, and buying stages; support roadmap development covering technical SEO, content optimization, AI answer visibility, entity authority, competitive share of voice, and always-on performance; partner with leadership to operationalize how SEO/AEO supports launches, campaigns, thought leadership, and web experiences. Lead the Team and Manage Execution: Manage, coach, and develop the SEO/AEO team — setting priorities, assigning ownership, managing capacity, and creating clarity around roles and decision-making. Build repeatable frameworks and governance models for keyword strategy, prompt tracking, technical audits, content briefs, launch measurement, AI visibility reporting, and competitive monitoring. Manage agency and vendor relationships for strategic output; raise the standard of SEO/AEO work across Veeam by educating stakeholders and embedding best practices into content, web, and campaign planning. Drive Technical SEO and Site Authority at Enterprise Scale: Own the technical SEO roadmap in partnership with Web, IT, UX, Engineering, Analytics, and Digital — prioritizing initiatives that improve crawlability, indexation, site speed, structured data, internal linking, information architecture, content discoverability, and conversion paths. Ensure Veeam's web ecosystem is built for both traditional search engines and AI-driven retrieval systems. Translate complex technical issues into business impact and secure cross-functional alignment for implementation. Build Veeam's AI Search and Answer-Engine Discipline: Define how Veeam measures and improves visibility across AI search and answer engines — supporting prompt strategy and partnering with Marketing Ops on AI visibility tracking, answer sentiment, citation analysis, competitive monitoring, and recommendation-rate measurement. Identify where Veeam is missing, misrepresented, under-cited, or under-recommended in AI-generated answers; partner cross-functionally to strengthen the authority signals AI systems rely on. Ensure Veeam content is structured to be clear, extractable, evidence-led, and aligned to how enterprise buyers ask questions. Connect Organic Discovery to Business Impact: Define and track KPIs across rankings, organic traffic, engagement, conversions, AI answer visibility, LLM recommendation rate, competitive share of voice, branded/non-branded discovery, and launch performance. Build performance narratives that help leadership understand what is working, where Veeam is under-indexing, and where additional focus is needed. Use data to influence content strategy, web priorities, campaign planning, and category narrative development. Influence Across the Organization: Act as a strategic partner to Web, Product Marketing, Demand Gen, PR/Comms, Brand, Analytics, and regional teams — bringing a clear point of view on how buyer behavior is changing as search shifts from links to answers and recommendations. Help stakeholders understand that SEO/AEO is a technical, content, authority, and measurement discipline — not a publishing checklist. Represent SEO/AEO priorities in planning, launch readiness, QBRs, and executive and strategic business reviews What You’ll Bring 7–9+ years in SEO, technical SEO, organic growth, digital strategy, or search — with 3+ years managing direct reports, developing talent, setting team priorities, and leading through ambiguity; background in global B2B tech, SaaS, cybersecurity, cloud, infrastructure, data, or enterprise software preferred. Strong technical SEO expertise across crawlability, indexation, rendering, structured data, site architecture, internal linking, redirects, canonicals, page speed, Core Web Vitals, international SEO, and enterprise CMS workflows. Strong understanding of AEO, GEO, AI search visibility, LLM-driven discovery, AI Overviews, answer engines, citation analysis, prompt tracking, entity optimization, and structured content. Proven ability to build SEO/AEO strategies that connect to business outcomes, not just traffic. Strong analytical skills and experience building dashboards, performance narratives, executive reporting, and KPI frameworks — with hands-on experience in seoClarity, GSC, GA4, Screaming Frog, Looker Studio, Tableau, Power BI, AEM, Jira, and Confluence. Skilled at influencing senior stakeholders and translating technical complexity into clear business recommendations; strong cross-functional leadership across content, web, product marketing, demand gen, PR, analytics, engineering, and agency partners. Experience supporting global launches, enterprise campaigns, thought leadership programs, and large-scale web/content optimization initiatives. Strategic, analytical, and operational mindset — able to connect big-picture direction to day-to-day execution in a fast-moving space where best practices are still evolving #LI-TS1 What you'll get Unlimited paid time off, 12 paid holidays including 4 global VeeaMe Days for self-care and 24 paid volunteer hours annually through Veeam Cares Paid parental leave: 8 weeks for all parents, 16 weeks for birthing parents Medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on your first day Mental health support, therapy sessions, and digital wellness tools via our Employee Assistance Program 401(k) retirement plan with company matching contributions Fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support through Maven, plus paid volunteer time AirVet: 24/7 virtual veterinary care at no cost Legal services, identity protection, and supplemental health insurance options Tax-advantaged spending accounts for healthcare, dependent care, and commuting Opportunities to learn and grow through on-demand libraries (LinkedIn Learning, O’Reilly), mentoring, workshops, and learning events like our annual Global Day of Learning Compensation Transparency Veeam is committed to pay transparency and equitable compensation. For this role, the compensation range below reflects the expected total target compensation (TTC), inclusive of base pay and a competitive performance-based bonus. For roles with a commission plan, the compensation range represents On Target Earnings (OTE), which includes base salary plus variable commission. When determining compensation, Veeam takes into consideration factors such as experience, education, skills, and geographic zone. Offers are typically made below the midpoint of the range. title: Senior Risk Analyst, Enterprise Risk Management
description: Location: For Those Who Work At Home, North Carolina Job Summary This role supports a Director in the Enterprise Risk Management function, including execution and facilitation of enterprise risk programs, GRC strategy, AI‑enabled risk transformation, forward‑looking risk reporting, and special projects for the office of the Chief Risk Officer. The role operates across disciplines including program execution, analytics, transformation, and executive communication; driving effectiveness and efficiency while supporting modernization across risk processes. Essential Functions Second Line of Defense Business Risk Team Support of ERM Risk Program Execution – Provide 2LOD Business Risk Team support to 2LOD teams through facilitation and execution of risk activities owned within the 2LOD including: risk and control self‑assessment (RCSA), business unit risk profile coordination, issues management, third party risk management, and regulatory change management. Assists the Director with the design and execution of ongoing risk monitoring routines and reporting within 2LOD. Forward‑Looking Risk Indicators & Board Reporting - Contribute to the quarterly refresh and enhancement of the CRO Forward‑Looking Indicator Dashboard, including data sourcing, trend analysis, construction, and review of executive‑ready visualizations for Board Risk Management Reports and CRO regulatory update materials. AI Integration for Risk Management - Support the design, prototyping, testing, and deployment of GenAI use cases for risk workflows, including tool design, prompt engineering, output validation, and human‑in‑the‑loop governance aligned to enterprise AI Risk Management standards. Strategic Risk Transformation Projects - Assist in facilitation and execution of transformation initiatives, including cross‑LOD stakeholder coordination, use case identification and design, dependency analysis, milestone tracking, and leadership status reporting. GRC Strategy, Layout & Archer Administration - Partner with Director and stakeholders on GRC platform strategy and reporting including business requirements, testing coordination, report development, and cross-team consulting. Policy, Procedure & Program Document Management - Draft, redline, and maintain enterprise risk program artifacts for all relevant activities, ensuring alignment to OCC Heightened Standards and internal governance requirements. Executive & Regulatory Communication – Assist in the production concise, board‑ready written and visual deliverables for the CRO, ELT, Board Risk Committee, OCC, and FRB, including top risk narratives, memos, and supervisory update materials. Cross‑Functional Coordination & Analytical Support – Support the team serving as integration point across ERM, Operational, Risk Compliance Risk, Credit Risk, Treasury Risk, Model Risk, Technology Risk, Strategy Risk, Internal Audit, and 1LOD partners on shared deliverables and enterprise campaigns relative to 2LOD-owned risks, controls, metrics, and findings. Hands‑on experience with Archer GRC (or equivalent enterprise GRC platform) across risk register, controls, findings, remediation plans, and reporting modules. Proven ability to draft, edit, and manage risk policies, programs, standards, and procedures aligned to regulatory expectations (OCC, FRB, FDIC). Strong executive communication skills - concise written narratives, board‑ready visualizations, and confident verbal engagement with senior leaders. Demonstrated experience managing multiple concurrent priorities under multiple concurrent deadlines. Project management proficiency with the ability to influence cross‑functional stakeholders and drive execution without direct authority.
